newsitem.title: UK: ICI Australia offer oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 11:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia offer oversubscribed. [CORRECTED 11:51 GMT]

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc said on Friday that the global offer of 143 million shares representing most of its (corrects to show that it is most, not all, of the stake affected) 62.4 percent stake in ICI Australia Ltd had been "significantly oversubscribed."
In a statement it said it had fixed an offer price of A$12.35 per share, with the retail price fixed at A$11.95.
The company said the offer price represented a discount of 2.76 percent to the A$12.70 closing price on the Australian stock exchange on Friday.

ICI said a related buy-back agreement on 30 million shares and an over-allotment option on a further 12 million shares would result in the divestment of all ICI's 185 million shares in ICI Australia if fully-taken up.

Total proceeds from the offering including the buy-back and over-allotment option were expected to be around A$2.2 billion, ICI said, resulting in an exceptional net profit of 475 million stg against third quarter results.

Proceeds from the sale of ICI's stake in the Australian company will be used to repay part of the borrowings used to fund its acquisition of Unilever Plc's specialty chemicals business for US$8 billion.
ICI chief executive Charles Miller Smith said "I am delighted with the success of the global offering of ICI's shareholding in ICI Australia and with the price we have achieved."
Shares in ICI were up two pence at 810-1/2 shortly after the announcement.
